records.normalizedEnglish: Temporarily arrest the flow of thought, affirm I am, imagine one’s real existence and self surrounded by favorable/protective thoughts. Practise evoking these images. When wishing to think alone, sit and repeat the previously described exclusion imagery. The text claims protection from external vibrations; this is historical belief, not detection of intrusion or a verified protective technique.

originalProcedureParaphrase: Temporarily arrest the flow of thought.
Affirm I am with an image of one’s real existence.
Imagine the self surrounded by favorable thoughts that the author says exclude external vibrations.
Practise these images; sit and use the same imagery when wishing to think alone.
records.guidedPublication: documentary-only; no verified protection or unwanted-intrusion claim

records.normalizedEnglish: The author explains changing opinions after relocation and waves of public sentiment by neighbors’ thought vibrations. Ordinary social influence examples do not establish this proposed mechanism.

When uncertain what to do, surround oneself with protective thoughts, described as a thought castle, and decide what is best. No decision scoring, timer, independent evidence or guarantee is supplied.

Author predicts greater interest and familiarity in a later meeting after attempted rapport, explicitly does not promise the other person necessarily does what is wanted at this stage. Repeat exercises without despair over failures; retain dignity/confidence and use gaze to allegedly restore rapport. Adapt principles to circumstances; no numeric frequency or mastery threshold.

Reread to find further ideas; coal/diamond and scriptural sayings are illustrations, not practical stages. Author introduces the next lesson’s attractive force of thought. Read between the lines does not license inventing missing historical instructions.
